conclusion: OTL1 compresses repetitive, textual and structured payloads strongly (highest mean ratio: zeros at 58.5×), leaves incompressible random data at roughly unit ratio (mean 0.984 (range 0.972–0.992)), and always round-trips byte-exactly. Because the compressed payload determines the number of packets, compression directly reduces screen time. OTL1 does not claim to beat zlib/zstd on general data; its purpose is a small, deterministic, inspectable instruction stream.

summary.note: OTL1 is a deterministic, dependency-free dictionary codec designed for the on-screen instruction set; zlib/zstd numbers are references, not part of the protocol. Each size is generated independently, so the random corpus is not compressible by block repetition.

title: Shared instruction dictionary (OTL1) compression effectiveness
